doc.title: Dave Bennett interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 16, 2025

title: Jazz academia and the uncertain music business
summary: Bennett is not in academia but is open to teaching, and admits the changing business sometimes scares him.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: So the current music scene is very interesting in jazz. You have this amazing level of jazz in academia. At the same time you hear people bemoaning about the fact that there’s not many jazz clubs and — are you involved in academia at all? Do you want to be?

I am not currently involved. I don’t know if I ever would be. If I were asked or if there was an opportunity for me to work in some capacity I don’t think I would turn it down you know. I don’t even know what would be involved in that, if you have to have a teaching certificate or what prep I would need to do to do something like that. I don’t know. I really don’t. Because I see the same thing you’re seeing. I mean the music business is so weird now, compared to the way it used to be. And it’s odd out there. I

mean I’ve been self-employed my whole life. And I’m grateful that financially I’ve done wonderful. But just because you’ve had success in the past doesn’t mean that it’s always going to happen. So there’s moments I get scared and I wonder how is this going to keep going. But it always seems to. So, you know, as far as teaching goes, I would like to do that more. I’ve had an occasional student or lesson here and there. But I’d like to do more of that if I can.
